stories.title: NTA lets JEE Main 2027 applicants start over with a fresh form
stories.summary: Candidates who made errors in their JEE Main 2027 Session 1 application can now submit a fresh form, even if they already have an application number or have paid the fee, the National Testing Agency has said. A second chance, at the price of a second form.

stories.title: Over 15,000 pharmacy seats lie empty in Maharashtra after counselling
stories.summary: Across 530 pharmacy colleges in Maharashtra, 31,521 students have taken admission out of 47,192 BPharm and PharmD seats on offer, despite multiple MHT CET CAP counselling rounds, Careers360 reports. That leaves more than 15,000 seats still waiting for takers.

stories.title: SRMJEEE 2027 will run in two phases
stories.summary: SRM Institute of Science and Technology will hold SRMJEEE 2027 phase 1 on 17 and 18 April and phase 2 on 19 and 20 June for BTech admissions. Application form filling starts soon, Careers360 reports.

stories.title: CLAT 2027 registration closes on 31 October
stories.summary: The Consortium of National Law Universities closes the CLAT 2027 registration portal on 31 October 2026, after a window open since 3 August. The exam covers admission to five-year integrated LLB and one-year LLM courses. Today is the day.

stories.title: Some universities now take 2027 undergraduate applications before Class 12 exams
stories.summary: Several universities, including Flame, Ashoka, MIT WPU and WPU Goa, have opened early application rounds for their 2027 undergraduate intake, Careers360 reports. Students can apply and complete entrance assessments before sitting their Class 12 board exams.

stories.title: Kerala releases its final NEET PG 2026 merit list
stories.summary: Kerala's Commissioner for Entrance Examinations released the final merit and category lists for PG medical admissions on 29 October. Candidates can check them on the CEE Kerala website and should watch for updates on option registration and allotment.

stories.title: AIAPGET 2026 counselling registration reopens until 3 November
stories.summary: The Ayush Admissions Central Counselling Committee has started online registration for AIAPGET PG Counselling 2026 Round 1, after the earlier schedule was put on hold on 27 October. Qualified candidates can register and fill choices until 3 November.

stories.title: Karnataka PGCET opens a final extended counselling round
stories.summary: The Karnataka Examinations Authority has announced a final extended round of counselling and seat allotment for PGCET 2026 admissions to MBA, MCA and MTech courses. Fresh option entry starts on 31 October.

stories.title: Symbiosis sets SLAT 2027 exam dates for December
stories.summary: Symbiosis International University has released the SLAT 2027 schedule. The final mock test is on 22 November, registration closes on 4 December, and the exams are on 19 and 26 December. Mock test registration needs to be done by 1 November.

stories.title: Australia hints at softening student visa rules after an A$2bn hit
stories.summary: Australia will fast-track visas for students forced overseas to finish their courses and may change how it assesses applicants' finances, amid record rejections from South Asia, Times Higher Education reports. Minister Julian Hill said the intent of the changes will not be watered down.

stories.title: Australia consults on the Genuine Student test and proof of funds
stories.summary: Australia's Department of Home Affairs is seeking views on reforms to the Genuine Student requirement and the financial capacity framework for student visa applicants. It says the aim is assurance that applicants come temporarily to study.

stories.title: What the India and New Zealand trade deal means for students
stories.summary: The India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement came into force on 20 October 2026. It brings new visa categories, longer post-study work rights for some graduates and a working holiday scheme for young Indians. Up to 5,000 new temporary employment visa holders may be in New Zealand at once.

stories.title: Memorial University's international enrolment falls 45%
stories.summary: Memorial University in Newfoundland and Labrador had 4,889 international students in 2023 and 2,682 in 2026, a 45% drop, as Canada continues to tighten study permits. University and provincial leaders are raising concerns about regional labour supply.

stories.title: English UK reviews student protection after school closures
stories.summary: English UK is consulting providers, agents and students on what protection students should get when an accredited English language school closes unexpectedly, aiming to agree a route and timetable before the end of 2026. Recent closures 'sent shockwaves', said chief executive Jodie Gray.

stories.title: Two UK English schools close, leaving hundreds of students to find new ones
stories.summary: Two English language training providers in the UK have closed in succession, forcing hundreds of international students to change their study plans. Those who already paid for tuition and accommodation are worried about how their money will be handled.

stories.title: International students who struggle most understand their health cover least
stories.summary: Research from Medibank and Nous Group, released at the Australian International Education Conference, found one in four international students in Australia struggle with health and wellbeing. Those in the poorest wellbeing groups knew least about services and their insurance.

stories.title: South Korea counts a record 2.66 million foreign residents
stories.summary: South Korea had 2,662,967 foreign residents as of November 2025, up 3.1% on a year earlier and the fourth straight annual rise, according to an interior ministry report. They now make up 5.1% of the population.

stories.title: South Korea will deport foreign students working as delivery riders
stories.summary: South Korea is stepping up crackdowns on foreigners working illegally as delivery riders, and international students caught working in restricted sectors will face forced deportation, the Ministry of Justice said. The student visa, it turns out, covers the lecture and not the scooter.

stories.title: Moldova admits 5.2% more foreign students
stories.summary: Moldova admitted more than 2,430 foreign students in 2026, about 5.2% more than the year before, preliminary education ministry data shows. Nearly 1,470 enrolled in bachelor's programmes. Students came from 31 countries, mainly Romania, Ukraine, India and Israel.

stories.title: International master's students explain why they went abroad
stories.summary: GMAC asked international master's students why they studied abroad. They cite new skills, alternate career paths and lifelong friends. The piece notes that subject, cost and location all weigh on the choice of where to go.

stories.title: FFE opens scholarships for first-year engineering, medical and law students
stories.summary: The Foundation for Excellence has invited applications for its 2026 to 27 scholarships for first-year Engineering, MBBS and Law students across India. Selected students receive ₹50,000 or more, based on merit and financial need. Applications are through FFE's online portal.

stories.title: AICTE extends its Industry Fellowship registration to 31 October
stories.summary: AICTE has extended Phase 2 registration for its Industry Fellowship Programme 2026 to 27 until 31 October. Industries and organisations can register at ifp.aicte.gov.in. The programme aims to bring technical institutions and industry partners closer.

stories.title: Gates Foundation opens its 2027 AI Fellow Program
stories.summary: The Gates Foundation is accepting applications until 11 November for its AI Fellow Program 2027, which seeks AI talent for work in global health, development and education. Fellows will join the first Africa-based cohort, working alongside the foundation's Africa team.

stories.title: Mozilla Foundation Fellowships offer up to $125,000
stories.summary: Applications are open until 17 December for the Mozilla Foundation Fellowships 2027 to 2028. Mozilla will award fellowships to builders working on technology it describes as too early, unexpected or ambitious for anyone else to fund.

stories.title: Macquarie's Road to Research Scholarship closes this month
stories.summary: Macquarie University in Sydney offers an AUD 40,900 living allowance and tuition coverage through its Road to Research Scholarship for Master of Research students starting full-time in Session 1 of 2027. Applicants must already live in Australia. Applications close this month.

stories.title: China University of Petroleum invites applicants for 2027 government scholarships
stories.summary: China University of Petroleum in Beijing is inviting applications for its 2027 Chinese Government Scholarship for master's and PhD study. Winners get a full tuition waiver, free accommodation, an annual stipend of ¥42,000 and medical insurance. Courses are taught in Chinese or English.

stories.title: University of Bonn offers workshop scholarships for PhD students
stories.summary: The Right Livelihood College campus at the University of Bonn is offering scholarships for PhD students from Africa, Asia and Latin America to join a workshop on sustainable use and conservation of natural resources. Applications close on 10 November 2026.

stories.title: The Global Burden of Disease Fellowship opens for 2027
stories.summary: The Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation at the University of Washington is accepting applications until 21 December for its GBD Fellowship 2027, an early-career, cohort-based postdoctoral programme for researchers who want careers in health metrics.

stories.title: Yale's Tobin Center takes pre-doctoral fellows on a rolling basis
stories.summary: Yale's Tobin Center and Economics Pre-Doctoral Fellows Program 2027 to 2028 is accepting applications on a rolling basis. It supports policy-relevant economics research and is aimed at graduates considering a PhD in economics or a related field.

stories.title: York University's Panther Promise covers full tuition
stories.summary: York University in Nebraska will cover full tuition for eligible incoming undergraduates from 2027 to 28 through grants, scholarships and university support. Students must qualify for a Federal Pell Grant and meet household income guidelines.

stories.title: Georgetown and UAB join the Association of American Universities
stories.summary: Georgetown University and the University of Alabama at Birmingham have joined the Association of American Universities, bringing its membership of leading research universities to 73, the AAU announced on Thursday. President Barbara R. Snyder welcomed both.

stories.title: Toronto tops Canada in the THE 2027 world rankings
stories.summary: Times Higher Education's 2027 World University Rankings place the University of Toronto first in Canada and 22nd globally. This year's tables include 2,297 institutions from 118 countries and territories. That is a lot of campuses to scroll past before finding your own.

stories.title: Binghamton is named SUNY's best value by the Princeton Review
stories.summary: The Princeton Review's Best Value Colleges rankings for 2027 place Binghamton University 19th among public institutions nationally for return on investment and career placement. It is the only SUNY university in the top 20.

stories.title: How rankings shape where students apply
stories.summary: The Daily Bruin looks at how college rankings influence students choosing among more than 3,700 US degree-granting institutions. U.S. News says dozens of staff weigh factors including completion rates, graduate earnings and school resources. Forbes and Niche offer alternatives.

stories.title: IIT Kanpur will run Uttar Pradesh's ₹104 crore cybersecurity centre
stories.summary: C3iHub, IIT Kanpur's cybersecurity innovation hub, will set up and operate the Uttar Pradesh Cyber Security Operations Centre. The ₹104.28 crore project has state cabinet approval and will provide round-the-clock monitoring of the state's government digital infrastructure.

stories.title: IIT Guwahati and Tata Electronics launch semiconductor courses
stories.summary: IIT Guwahati has teamed up with Tata Electronics to strengthen education, skills and research in semiconductor assembly, testing, marking and packaging. The programmes will be designed around what the industry says it needs.

stories.title: Universities of Wisconsin enrolment slips as international numbers fall
stories.summary: The Universities of Wisconsin enrolled 164,579 students in fall 2026, down 1,233 from last year. Most of the decline came from international enrolment, which fell by 1,134 to 8,889, according to the system.

stories.title: MBRSC and the University of Sharjah sign a space research MoU
stories.summary: The Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre and the University of Sharjah will explore joint research in space science and engineering and collaborate on scientific forums and knowledge sharing. The agreement was signed by MBRSC Director General Salem Humaid AlMarri.

stories.title: Dartmouth students say they use AI to learn, and suspect their peers do not
stories.summary: The inaugural Dartmouth AI Survey of more than 1,500 Dartmouth students and 1,000 college students nationwide found most say they use AI mainly for learning, not cutting corners, but believe their peers do. Everyone is honest, apparently, except everyone else.

stories.title: Some Penn professors go analog to cope with AI
stories.summary: Some University of Pennsylvania faculty are reducing technology in class in response to AI, with some banning laptops and phones entirely. Urban Studies co-director Julia McWilliams has gone almost entirely analog for one class, with field notebooks and printed readings.

stories.title: 15 percent of US undergraduates have tried digital wagering, survey finds
stories.summary: Inside Higher Ed surveys found 15 percent of undergraduates have used online sportsbooks, prediction markets or other digital wagering since enrolling, rising to 25 percent of men. Most institutions are not tracking the issue on their campuses.

stories.title: US Justice Department makes arrests in a FAFSA 'ghost student' scheme
stories.summary: The Justice Department charged several people and seized more than $750,000 in cryptocurrency from a Kenyan account in a nationwide investigation into federal student aid fraud. The arrests are the first results from Operation Ghostbusters, aimed at fake student enrolments.

stories.title: Jamia will resume offline classes on 10 November
stories.summary: Jamia Millia Islamia will restart offline classes from 10 November after 18 days of protests over the students' union constitution. Second-semester exams for all UG and PG programmes will run from 16 to 21 November, in offline mode only.

stories.title: Supreme Court reserves verdict on counting PhD years as teaching experience
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has reserved its verdict on whether time spent earning an MPhil or PhD can count as teaching experience for Associate Professor posts under the UGC Regulations, 2018. The question arose in appeals over an appointment at Kannur University.

stories.title: NHRC asks for a full report on Delhi student hostels
stories.summary: After the Satya Niketan building collapse, the NHRC has issued notices to the Delhi government and the UGC seeking a comprehensive report on hostels and student accommodation, in consultation with Delhi University. It wants existing hostels assessed as well as new ones considered.

stories.title: Contract faculty at 12 Telangana universities seek regularisation
stories.summary: Contract teachers across Telangana's 12 state universities have demanded regularisation, Seventh PRC and UGC pay scales and job security until absorption, Deccan Chronicle reports. They want a decision before the government proceeds with recruitment.

stories.title: Bangladesh's UGC plans a satellite TV channel for higher education
stories.summary: Bangladesh's University Grants Commission is planning a dedicated satellite television channel for higher education to reduce disparities in access, chairman Mamun Ahmed said. A pilot may use Bangladesh Open University's existing facilities.

stories.title: Wales promised a student mental health standard and got a framework
stories.summary: A Wonkhe analysis argues that Wales's Common Mental Health and Wellbeing Framework, published in August, sets no minimum standard and creates no requirements for universities, despite a 2023 Senedd committee call accepted by the government. Its steering group had no student on it.

stories.title: Higher education's strategic plans take too long, argues an Inside Higher Ed essay
stories.summary: Strategic planning at universities traditionally takes two academic years of committees, forums and drafts, an Inside Higher Ed essay notes. It argues the pace of change now outruns that process, and that plans projecting 10 to 25 years ahead have become wishful thinking.

stories.title: Foreign universities are coming, and a professor asks if Indian ones are ready
stories.summary: In a Daily Excelsior column, Prof R K Uppal argues that the entry of foreign universities into India promises global exposure and research collaboration, but asks whether Indian universities, which grew mainly by adding numbers, are ready to compete.

research.title: Reconstructing Missing Mandi Prices in North-East India with Regional Factors
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Agricultural price panels contain prolonged and clustered reporting gaps, yet their reconstruction is often evaluated by deleting isolated observations. We investigate a regional-factor approach to weekly mandi-price reconstruction in five North-East Indian states, with Bihar and. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: After One-Click Video: The Inflow of Service-Type Content, the Failure of the Recommendation Pool Mechanism, and the BoLe System
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: In September 2026, a new large language model was released. Soon after, a new way of making explainer videos became very popular: people asked the model to write a program, and the program produced the video. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Balancing Mobility Efficiency and Environmental Exposure During Mega Events: A Multi-agent Routing Framework
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mega events can generate concentrated travel demand, intensifying congestion around venues and increasing travelers' environmental exposure. Existing traffic management strategies focus on travel efficiency, with limited attention to exposure risks. Taking mega-event travel as a short-term. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Bouba Beats Kiki, and Other Regularities in the Subjective Preferences of LLMs
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Users engage with large language models on tasks that are purely objective ("When was Netflix founded?"), purely subjective ("What should I name my child?") or anywhere in-between. We have rich tools for evaluating model accuracy with. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: DeflectBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Rhetorical Fallacy Generation in LLMs
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether large language models can be prompted to generate rhetorical fallacies on demand, and whether current safety post-training constrains this behavior, has received less attention than the related question of detecting fallacies in existing text. We. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: From the Gettier Machine to Justified True Output: A Three-Step Account of Rational Trust in Generative AI
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) settles into everyday practices of inquiry, an old epistemological question returns in a new guise: when does a proposition a user takes from an AI output become something the user knows. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: GPU-Resident Speculative Decoding for In-Browser LLM Inference with WebGPU
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: WebGPU enables private, offline LLM inference inside web pages, but browser dispatch, inter-process communication, synchronous readback and single-token kernels slow decoding and make conventional speculative decoding inefficient. We present a WebGPU runtime that addresses these browser-specific. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: IKTRACE: A Natural Language Processing Framework for Identifying Indigenous Knowledge Representation in Academic Literature
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: As artificial intelligence systems increasingly rely on vast textual data, respectful and accurate representation of Indigenous Knowledge has become critical. This paper introduces IKTRACE, a natural language processing framework for identifying, analyzing, and organizing Indigenous Knowledge. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
